01.words: Citizens of this country, thank you for having me. I come with a plain belief that this country is on the edge of something good. The founders did not trust power, and they were right not to. I mean to use this office's power sparingly, and to give back what it does not need. // A new day is beginning, and I would like us to meet it with a little more faith than we have lately allowed ourselves. The oath is a promise to the future as much as to the present, and the future is a thing I am looking forward to.

04.words:
First thing on February 4th, Alina Olson walks up to you in the street. Your mother has news for you. // Alina Olson: I'm about as conservative as they come. [Replies: I see it the same way. | I see it differently. | I'm glad you told me. | I keep mine to myself, mostly.] // Alina Olson: BLAIR OLSON
I see it the same way.
Glad I'm not the only one.
We'll talk more later.

06.words:
First thing on January 16th, at work, you talk with Isaiah Calderon.
Isaiah Calderon read what Meridian News Network printed on collective bargaining for public workers, and it has been on their mind since. // Isaiah Calderon: Meridian News Network ran a story on the change on collective bargaining for public workers taking effect. I thought of you when I read it. [Replies: I read it too. I didn't love it, but it's fair. | It sounded like somebody who has never had to live with it. | Which part got to you? | Let me get settled first, and then you can tell me.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
I read it too. I didn't love it, but it's fair.
Then what do we do about it? [Replies: Yeah. I think it does matter. I just didn't want to say so. | We can both read it and not agree. | I'll think about it. I have to go.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
Yeah. I think it does matter. I just didn't want to say so.
So why isn't anyone doing anything about collective bargaining for public workers? We're the ones who live with it. [Replies: All right, you're right. It bothers me too. | I saw it. They only told one side of collective bargaining for public workers, and that's the side people will remember. | Let me read it again before I say anything else.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
All right, you're right. It bothers me too.
Does that mean you'd say something, if someone asked? [Replies: I read it twice. I still don't buy it. | I'm sorry. I can't get into this right now.] // Isaiah Calderon: BLAIR OLSON
I read it twice. I still don't buy it.
That's not how I read it. Where did they go wrong?
Don't be surprised if I ask you again.

07.words:
First thing on January 23rd, you meet Daniel Banks downtown.
Daniel Banks answered the governor from the floor, and now comes down the aisle to find you. // Daniel Banks: Blair, a word. I answered the governor today, and I wanted you to hear why from me.
I said what a lot of us were thinking. Where does that leave you? [Replies: Some of it I liked and some of it I didn't. I'm not going to pretend it was all one thing. | What would you do instead? That's the part I didn't hear. | I'll hear you out before the vote. That's a promise. | I'll vote the way my district needs, not the way either of you asks.] // Daniel Banks: BLAIR OLSON
Some of it I liked and some of it I didn't. I'm not going to pretend it was all one thing.
I appreciate your honesty, even where we differ.

08.words:
Susan Griffin: First thing on October 30th, you step into the Secretary of State's office and ask for Susan Griffin. // Susan Griffin: Can I help you? [Replies: I want to run for U.S. Senator. November 3, 2026 · Held by Allison Craig | I want to run for U.S. Representative (District 4). November 3, 2026 · Held by Jessica Rivera] // Susan Griffin: BLAIR OLSON
I want to run for U.S. Senator.
Running for U.S. Senator? Good. Let me pull the papers. You'd serve 6 years. First comes the primary, March 10, 2026, and then the general, November 3, 2026. It's a statewide office. Every voter in the state gets a say in who holds it. The papers are due back December 26.
You have to be at least 30. [Replies: Alright.]

09.words:
First thing on October 28th, you sit down at home with Adam Olson.
Adam Olson has been reading who filed for Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce before you did. // Adam Olson: Blair, sit down a second.
You're not first in: incumbent Susan Jensen filed for Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce ahead of you. [Replies: Do you know much about Susan Jensen? | Then I'd better get to work. | Let them run. | Thanks for telling me.] // Adam Olson: BLAIR OLSON
Do you know much about Susan Jensen?
Not much. Only what was filed. [Replies: Good. Now it's a real race. | Doesn't change anything for me. | I need a minute.] // Adam Olson: BLAIR OLSON
Good. Now it's a real race.
That's the spirit.
